reason: I'd clone the open-source version and try it on a side repo the week it hits HN, sure. But paying $99 a month for a hosted server from a pre-alpha one-person project, to let agents loose on client code overnight? No.
objection: Agents running unattended on our client repos all night is a security risk. Budgets and loop guards stop runaway cost. They don't stop an agent leaking secrets or pushing something bad while nobody is watching.
would_change_my_mind: A clear sandboxing story (no network or secrets access by default, reviewed permissions per flow) plus a few months of other agencies running it in production without incidents.
